Lithium niobate is a well-known coating material with a wide band gap and stability against sulfide electrolytes.
Lithium zirconate is expected to be stable and insulating, with compatibility against sulfur-containing electrolytes.
Lithium titanate is a good lithium-ion conductor with high stability and a suitable band gap for insulation.
Lithium metasilicate is likely to be stable and insulating, potentially offering good interface compatibility.
Lithium triborate is a glass-forming borate expected to have a high band gap and good chemical stability.
Lithium fluoride is a halide with a very wide band gap and high stability against oxidation at high voltage.
Calcium lithium silicate may offer good stability and insulation due to the presence of calcium and silicate groups.
Lithium titanium phosphate combines phosphate and titanate chemistry, potentially yielding favorable stability and ion conductivity.
